Module com.example.demo
Package com.example.miniproyecto4.controller

Class GameController

java.lang.Object
com.example.miniproyecto4.controller.GameController
public class GameController extends Object
Controller for GameView.fxml. Receives the human's already-placed Board from PlayerController (see initializePlayerData(com.example.miniproyecto4.model.Board, java.util.List<com.example.miniproyecto4.model.Ship>, java.lang.String)), builds a random MachinePlayer opponent, and runs the whole shooting phase: clicks on girdIa fire at the machine; every human miss hands the turn to a background MachineTurnThread; a GameTimerThread keeps a running match clock; "Guardar partida" persists both the flat-file record and the full serialized state.

  • Constructor Details

    • GameController

      public GameController()
      Creates the collaborators this controller owns for the lifetime of a match: the cell-view lookup maps for both grids, the persistence helpers, and the shared turn lock. The actual match data (boards, opponents, player stats) is supplied afterward by either initializePlayerData or resumeGame, since FXMLLoader must be able to call this constructor with no arguments.

  • Method Details

    • initializePlayerData

      public void initializePlayerData(Board placedBoard, List<Ship> fleet, String name)
      Injected by PlayerController right after navigating here. Draws the human fleet on gridUser, spins up a random machine opponent, and starts the match clock.
      Parameters:
      placedBoard - the board the player configured in PlayerController
      fleet - the same fleet instance, already placed
      name - the name typed by the player

    • resumeGame

      public void resumeGame(SerializableGameState state)
      Injected by HomeController instead of initializePlayerData(com.example.miniproyecto4.model.Board, java.util.List<com.example.miniproyecto4.model.Ship>, java.lang.String) when the player chose "Continuar" on the home screen. Rebuilds both opponents from the serialized boards (fleets, hits and misses included) and repaints both grids to match exactly where the match was left off, instead of starting a fresh one.
      Parameters:
      state - the snapshot loaded by GameStateSerializer
